# Using Leak Guard in Claude / Claude Code

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Claude / Claude Code.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.claude/skills/leak-guard/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.claude/skills/leak-guard/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness claude --skill leak-guard
node packages/cli install --harness claude --skill leak-guard --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Claude / Claude Code loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also run it explicitly by typing `/leak-guard`.

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.claude/skills/leak-guard` for a project install, or `~/.claude/skills/leak-guard` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `leak-guard` is listed.

## Notes

- Nested .claude/skills folders inside subdirectories also load when working there.
- This skill drives packages/leakguard. Read scripts/leakguard.root for the absolute package path; if you copied the skill folder by hand without the install command, locate packages/leakguard in the gti-skills repository and use its bin/leakguard.mjs and bin/leakguard-hook.mjs paths.
- The guard installs as a command hook (PreToolUse) in .claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json.
- Documentation: [Claude / Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) (path source: official).
